function.description: Search file paths using a glob pattern (examples: "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx").
function.name: glob

hidden.description: Include hidden files and directories (default: false).

limit.description: Maximum number of matching files to return (default: 100)

path.description: Directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files against

function.description: Search file contents using ripgrep's regular expression syntax or literal text matching. Use it to locate specific code, symbols, or text patterns, and narrow searches with `path` or `include`. Returns matching file paths, line numbers, and line previews.
function.name: grep

include.description: Glob pattern to filter files (for example, "*.js" or "*.{ts,tsx}")

limit.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return (default: 100)

literal.description: Treat `pattern` as exact text instead of a regular expression (default: false).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

pattern.description: Regular expression or literal text to match in file contents.

function.description: Read the contents of a file or directory. Supports text files, images, and PDFs. Images and PDFs are presented directly to the model. Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.
function.name: read

limit.description: The maximum number of lines or directory entries to read (defaults to and capped at 2000)

offset.description: The line or directory entry to start reading from (1-based)

function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Commands run on Linux using bash. Quote file paths containing spaces or special characters. Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.
function.name: shell

background.description: Run the command in the background and return immediately (useful for dev servers and long-running builds). You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT poll for completion.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable the timeout. Defaults to 120000 for foreground commands. Background commands have no timeout by default.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

function.description:
Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.
function.name: skill

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

function.description:
Fetch content from an HTTP or HTTPS URL and return it as text, markdown, or HTML. Markdown is the default.

Use a more targeted tool when one is available. This tool is read-only. Large text results may be replaced with a preview while the complete output is retained in managed storage.
function.name: webfetch

format.description: The format to return the content in. Defaults to markdown.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch content from
